The physical internet starts here.

IONA builds autonomous networks that move goods the way the internet moves information - instantly, affordably, and everywhere. We provide the full technology stack so logistics operators can deliver what was previously undeliverable.

See how it works

Trusted by operators, agencies, and partners across Europe

One stack.
Full autonomy.
Your brand.

IONA provides everything a logistics operator needs to launch autonomous delivery — without building an aviation organisation from scratch. Aircraft, ground infrastructure, operations software, and regulatory compliance. Fully integrated. Fully white-label. The operator owns the service, the data, and the customer relationship. IONA is the infrastructure layer.

Up to 20 parcels to 200 km, on a single autonomous flight.

Information became instant. Energy became distributed. Goods are next.

The internet made information programmable - any device to any device, anywhere.

Solar and batteries did the same for energy.

Physical goods are still trapped in schedules, routes, and vehicles that favour density over access.

30%

of the world's population lives in areas where a simple delivery costs 3 to 10 times more than in urban centres.

IONA is building the infrastructure that changes this. Autonomous networks that connect people, businesses, and communities to the goods they need - reliably, affordably, and wherever they are.

Minutes, not hours.

IONA turns inaccessible routes into routine operations.
Long-range autonomous flight that plugs directly into logistics networks – delivering what used to take hours in minutes.

Example Scenarios:

Island clinic to mainland hospital

4–8 hours by ferry → 6 min with IONA.

Rural pharmacy resupply

Next-day van, weather permitting → 22 minutes, any day with IONA.

Industrial spare part

45-minute van dispatch → 12 minutes, on demand with IONA.

See what IONA changes for your network

relevant_companies.polished_summary: Ionadrones is a pioneering company that builds autonomous networks for logistics, enabling the efficient movement of goods akin to how the internet transmits information. Their comprehensive technology stack includes innovative products such as the Sonnet tilt-rotor aircraft, an Autonomy Operating System, and various software solutions designed for logistics operators across industries like healthcare, e-commerce, and maritime. By providing advanced tools for mission planning, compliance, and real-time monitoring, Ionadrones empowers logistics operators to deliver previously undeliverable goods swiftly and affordably.

relevant_companies.company_summary: Medical Drone Delivery specializes in autonomous VTOL drone technology, offering innovative solutions for sectors such as ports, energy, defense, emergency services, and critical infrastructure. Their core products include the Aera drone, designed for efficient long-range flights, and the Avy Dock, a purpose-built docking station that supports unmanned operations. With a focus on enhancing aerial coverage and operational efficiency, the company caters to organizations that require reliable and scalable drone solutions for various applications.

Frequently asked questions

Frequently asked questions

Answers to your questions, every step of the way.

What is the Avy Drone Network?

It's a complete system — drone, docking station, software and control centre — that works together as one. The drone launches automatically, flies itself, and returns to its dock to recharge, all without anyone needing to be on site. Think of it as always-on aerial coverage, ready to deploy in seconds.

What makes Avy different from a regular drone?

Most drones need a pilot standing nearby. Avy is designed to operate fully remotely and autonomously — beyond visual line of sight, in real weather conditions, over long distances. It's closer to an unmanned aircraft system than a consumer drone.

What can the Avy drone carry?

The Aera carries payloads up to 3kg as standard. That covers most cameras, sensors and medical kits. For heavier or custom payloads, we work with you directly.

How far and how fast can it fly?

The Aera covers up to 100km on a single charge at a cruise speed of 100km/h, with a typical flight time of around 60 minutes.

Can it fly in bad weather?

Yes. The Aera handles rain, strong winds up to 35+ knots, extreme cold and heat. It's built for operational conditions, not just ideal ones.

Where is Avy based and where do you operate?

We're based in Amsterdam, Netherlands. We operate across Europe and beyond — from ports and coastlines to remote regions in Africa and the Middle East.

## Get an answer faster

Quick answers to the things you’re wondering so you can carry on.

What is the best way to get in touch about a drone deployment?
[icon]

Fill in the business form on this page and a member of the Avy team will respond within one working
day. For urgent enquiries, email fly@avy.eu directly.

Where does Avy operate?
[icon]

Avy is based in Amsterdam and operates drone networks across Europe. We work with clients in the
Netherlands and internationally — if you have a specific location in mind, get in touch and we can
discuss what's possible.

How long does it take to get a drone network operational?
[icon]

It depends on the complexity of the deployment and the regulatory environment in your country. For
operations in the Netherlands, Avy holds a BVLOS LUC which significantly reduces lead time. For
international deployments, regulatory engagement typically adds time to the process. Contact us
early — the sooner we understand your requirements, the sooner we can give you a realistic timeline.

Does Avy offer a demonstration or proof of concept?
[icon]

Yes. Avy has conducted proof of concept programmes with clients across emergency response, ports,
and defence. If you want to understand what autonomous drone operations look like in practice before
committing to a full deployment, a scoped PoC is often the right starting point.

I'm interested in working at Avy — who should I contact?
[icon]

All open roles and application instructions are on the careers page. If you have a specific question
before applying, include it in your application or email fly@avy.eu with the subject line "Careers
enquiry."

I'm a journalist or researcher — how do I reach the press team?
[icon]

Email fly@avy.eu with "Press" in the subject line and a member of the team will get back to you.

# Drone networks

Most drone operations depend on a pilot being present at every flight. Avy's approach is different.
Docking stations are placed at fixed locations, near critical infrastructure, nature reserves,
ports, or any area requiring persistent aerial coverage. The aircraft takes off, lands, charges, and
shelters in its dock autonomously, ready to fly again within 30 seconds of a mission being
triggered.

Multiple docking stations create a drone network. A single operator, monitoring remotely from a
command centre, can manage coverage across hundreds of square kilometres with no one on site at any
individual location.

This is what makes continuous autonomous aerial operations possible at scale.

## Did we miss anything?

Here are a few of the frequently asked questions

What is a drone network?
[icon]

A drone network is a system of aircraft, docking stations and operations software working together.
Each docking station handles launch, landing and recharging automatically. A central operations
centre connects them, allowing one operator to manage missions across multiple locations
simultaneously.

Can the network be expanded over time?
[icon]

Yes. The system is modular — additional docking stations and aircraft can be added to extend
coverage without replacing existing infrastructure. The operations software scales to manage a
growing number of nodes from the same interface.

Does Avy operate the network or do we?
[icon]

Both options are available. Avy operates drone networks on behalf of clients across Europe under its
BVLOS LUC. Organisations can also purchase the system and operate it themselves, with training
provided through the Avy Flight Academy.

How many docking stations does a network need?
[icon]

It depends on the coverage required. A single station covers up to 7,850km² — enough for most port,
nature reserve or infrastructure monitoring use cases. For corridor coverage or city-scale
operations, multiple stations are deployed and managed from one centre.

Where can I find the full specifications?
[icon]

Full specifications for the Aera aircraft, docking station and payload are on their individual
pages. You can also download the complete spec sheet and product brochure using the form on this
page.

What payloads does the Aera carry?
[icon]

The Aera carries up to 3kg across a range of payload configurations including thermal cameras, RGB
cameras, and the Avy MedBox for medical cargo. Payloads can be swapped between missions.

## The only long-range VTOL built for remote operations

##### Unmanned aviation

Aera is a robust VTOL, fixed wing drone. It takes off and lands vertically like a helicopter before

## Fundamentally fixed-wing

Most drones are multirotors. They hover using rotors, which is simple and versatile but extremely
inefficient over distance. A comparable multicopter covers 7km on a single charge. The Avy Aera
covers 100km.

The difference is lift. Fixed-wing aircraft generate lift aerodynamically as they move through the
air, using a fraction of the energy a multicopter needs to stay airborne. The Aera uses this
principle to cover long distances efficiently — cruising at 23 m/s (83 km/h) on a single 1 kWh
battery for up to 75 minutes.

For organisations that need aerial coverage across large areas — ports, energy networks, coastlines,
rail corridors — this is the difference between a drone that works and one that doesn't.

## Takes off anywhere, flies like a plane.

Fixed-wing aircraft traditionally need a runway or a catapult to launch and a net or a runway to
land. This makes them impractical for most operational environments. The Avy Aera solves this with
four VTOL rotors that lift the aircraft vertically from any flat surface, transition it to
fixed-wing cruise flight, and return it to a vertical landing.

The result is an aircraft that combines the operational simplicity of a multicopter with the range
and speed of a fixed-wing plane. It launches from a docking station, a rooftop, a ship deck, or an
open field. No runway. No catapult. No net.

The Aera is designed to fly in conditions that ground most commercial drones. Wind resistance of 30

maintain accurate airspeed measurement in cold and wet conditions.

It is not a fair-weather system.

## Designed for repeat missions

Aera carries a suite of safety systems developed for operations over critical infrastructure and
populated areas. The QuadChute parachute recovery system deploys automatically in the event of a
critical failure, satisfying the ground risk mitigation requirements for BVLOS operations. A flight
termination system, return-to-land, rally points, and enhanced containment give operators multiple
layers of contingency.

ADS-B In and Out allows the aircraft to detect and be detected by manned aviation. Remote ID
broadcasts the aircraft's identity and position in compliance with EU regulations.

Dual LTE command and control with direct radio backup means the aircraft maintains its connection in
environments where a single link would be unreliable.

## Did we miss anything?

Here are a few of the frequently asked questions

What is a VTOL drone?
[icon]

VTOL stands for vertical takeoff and landing. A VTOL drone launches and lands vertically like a
helicopter, without needing a runway, catapult, or recovery net. The Avy Aera is a fixed-wing VTOL —
it takes off vertically, transitions to efficient fixed-wing cruise flight, and lands vertically.
This gives it the range of a fixed-wing aircraft with the operational simplicity of a multicopter.

How far can Aera fly?
[icon]

On a standard 1 kWh battery, Aera covers 100km at standard weight and 80km at maximum takeoff
weight. With the extended battery, range increases to 200km (170km at MTOW). Flight time is 75
minutes on a standard battery and over 120 minutes on the extended battery.

What is the difference between Aera and a multicopter?
[icon]

Range and efficiency. A multicopter generates lift using rotors, which consumes a lot of energy. A
comparable multicopter covers around 7km on a single charge. The Aera generates lift aerodynamically
using its wings, covering 100km on a single charge — roughly 14 times further. For industrial
applications covering large areas, this difference is decisive.

Can Aera fly in rain and wind?
[icon]

Yes. Multiple docking stations are managed from a single remote command centre. Additional docks can
be added to extend coverage along a corridor or across a wider area without replacing existing
infrastructure.

What payloads does Aera carry?
[icon]

Aera carries up to 3kg in an 8-litre payload bay. Available configurations include thermal and RGB
sensor payloads, the Avy MedBox for medical cargo, and AI compute modules for onboard processing.
With the QuadChute parachute installed, payload capacity is 2kg. Payloads can be swapped between
missions without tools.

Is Aera BVLOS capable?
[icon]

Yes. Aera is designed specifically for BVLOS operations. It carries ADS-B In/Out, Remote ID, dual
LTE command and control with direct radio backup, and a QuadChute parachute recovery system that
meets BVLOS ground risk mitigation requirements. Avy operates Aera under its BVLOS LUC — one of
Europe's first.

Does Aera need a pilot on site?
[icon]

No. Paired with the Avy Dock, Aera launches, executes its mission, and returns to charge fully
autonomously. The remote pilot operates from anywhere with an internet connection. No ground crew is
required at the deployment site.

## No ground crew

Most drone operations require a team on the ground. A pilot to launch, a ground crew to recover the
aircraft, someone to manage charging. The Avy Dock eliminates all of it.

The door opens, the landing pad extends, the aircraft launches. On return, precision RTK GPS guides
the Aera back to within centimetres of the landing pad, the door closes, and charging begins
automatically. The remote pilot operates from anywhere with an internet connection.

## Built for the conditions

The dock is designed to operate where conditions are less than perfect; coastlines, industrial
ports, critical infrastructure, and environments where temperatures drop below zero in winter and
exceed 40°C in summer.

The enclosure handles static winds up to 55 knots (102 km/h) and precipitation up to 50mm/h. The
internal HVAC system maintains the aircraft within operating temperature across an ambient range of
-15°C to 50°C. Dehumidification runs automatically during storage.

The dock does not need a hangar, a shelter, or a climate-controlled room. It is the shelter.

## Did we miss anything?

Here are a few of the frequently asked questions

What is an autonomous docking station?
[icon]

A docking station is a ground unit that handles everything a ground crew would — launching,
recovering, charging, and sheltering the aircraft between missions. The Avy Dock does this without
any operator present at the site. The remote pilot manages missions from a command centre via a 4G,
5G, or wired data link.

Can the dock operate in cold or hot climates?
[icon]

Yes. The internal HVAC system maintains the aircraft and electronics within operating temperature
across an ambient range of -15°C to 50°C. It has been deployed in sub-zero winter conditions and in
high-temperature industrial environments.

How quickly can the dock launch the aircraft?
[icon]

From standby to launch in 30 seconds. The door opens, the landing pad extends, and the aircraft is
airborne. No setup, no briefing, no ground crew required.

Can multiple docks be networked together?
[icon]

Yes. Multiple docking stations are managed from a single remote command centre. Additional docks can
be added to extend coverage along a corridor or across a wider area without replacing existing
infrastructure.

What happens if the data connection is lost?
[icon]

The dock maintains dual LTE connectivity with a wired RJ45 Ethernet backup. The aircraft also has
onboard failsafe behaviour — in the event of a lost link it follows a pre-defined contingency
procedure, typically returning to the dock.

Does someone need to be on site to operate the dock?
[icon]

No. The dock is designed for fully unmanned operation. Personnel can access the platform safely when
required — the dock has warning lights, audible alerts, and five emergency stop buttons — but
day-to-day operation requires no one on site.

## SD-03

## Servo Drive for UAVs with Take-Off Weight Less then 60 kg

### APPLICATION

Servo drive SD3 is designed for:
* UAVs with takeoff weight less then 60 kg
* Conversion of manned aircraft into UAV
* Equipping of manned aircrafts with automatic piloting system (APS)
* Power movement of UAV control surfaces and elements

### SENSORS

Servo drive condition monitoring:
* Temperature of the board power stage
* Amperage
* Voltage
* Data from the absolute encoder

# SAT-i

## Solar-Powered SAT-i aircraft can perform
## a continuous flight throughout
## the daylight hours

Gallery ][15]
Video ][16]

### OVERVIEW

The **SAT-i** is a fixed-wing unmanned aircraft with full automatic takeoff, landing and mission
modes.

Take-off is hand-launched UAV but the mission and the landing are performed in automatic mode with a
touchdown accuracy of about 100 m on a 200m long landing zone.

Diagnostics, flight mission planning and remote control can be performed through the wireless
network connection.

Proprietary Autopilot.

Command link: up to 60 km
Video transmission: up to 60 km (optional)
The Iridium backup command link is of unlimited range.

**Application:**
* Mapping
* Video surveillance and monitoring
* NDVI index agroculture
* Payload (max. 0.6 kg)
* Radio link relay

# DRONE-CAPTURE
# NET SYSTEM

## For Capturing And Retrieving Small Drones

Video ][15]

Firing a net at a drone stops the drone by prohibiting the rotor blades.

### OVERVIEW

The drone-capture net system for small drones is designed to capture and retrieve the UAV to the
point of destination. The capture is executed with a 6,000 x 6,000 mm net shot towards the drone
from the UAV carrier.

### ADVANTAGES

Nabbing a drone out of the sky offers a few advantages over attempting to jam it or blowing it up:
* You avoid bringing laser-riddled drones crashing down on urban crowds.
* You don’t foul up cellular communications networks.
* You get more out of forensic analysis, which can show who launched the drone and from where.

### APPLICATIONS

The drone-capture net system is ideal for securing:
* Airports
* Prisons
* Military bases
* Government buildings

# GROUND CONTROL STATION
# GCS.A

## 20' container

Gallery ][15]
Video ][16]

### OVERVIEW

The GCS.A is installed into a modified 20-foot container, enhanced with a generator section.

The GCS.A unmanned systems command center provides everything required for operators to undertake
missions in complete comfort and safety, including climate control, redundant power and
communications.

State-of-the-art features and amenities include:
* Autonomous operating time up to 48 hours
* Housing for the communication and control equipment
* Three workplaces for the pilots and the payload operators
* Directional antenna for telemetry and communication
* Directional antenna for video and data links
* Support Equipment for the unmanned aerial system (transport module)

### SPECIFICATIONS

**Temperature range:**

-40°F to +131°F (-40°C to +55°C)

**Dimensions:**

Length 295 in (7500 mm), width 98 in (2492 mm), height 102 in (2585 mm)

**Transportation:**

truck tractor

**Generator:**

15 kW

**Autonomous operating time:**

48 h

**Automated workplaces:**

2+1

The GCS.A is divided into technical sections:
* Control compartment (operator);
* Service and supply compartment;
* Generator compartment.

**Design options**

Customization is possible upon request.

**Control compartment (operator)**

Equipped with two Automated Workstations (AWS). The first is the workplace for the operator of the
UAV, the second – for the operator of the payload.

Each AWS is equipped with a control panel, three monitors (two main and one auxiliary) connected to
a separate computer. The panel can be customized/adapted for a tactical or operational radio
station, intercom and other equipment.

A central console controls the air conditioning and is equipped with 220V connectors, 5V USB ports
and speakers.

**The repair and technical compartment:**

— shelves and workbenches can be adjusted in height
— a water closet equipped with a 17 gallon (65 liters) water tank, a faucet and a bio-toilet bowl)
— an air conditioning system

**The control compartment:**

— ground station control panel
— power supply cabinet with PC
— continuous power supply
— a heater, recuperator, an internal air-conditioning module, a minibar with kettle and a coffee
machine, a mini-fridge, a filing cabinet make for a comfortable stay in the compartment even over
long periods of time

**The generator compartment is equipped with:**

— a 15 kW power generator,
— external air conditioning modules,
— a telescopic pneumatic mast,
— an AC/DC transformer,
— a power generator control cabinet,
— batteries for continuous operation of the 27 V electric power supply.

# UAV-170 Engine

### OVERVIEW

The UAV-170 engine based on the Fiala PROP. company FM 170 B2 – FS power plant is a 4-stroke
gasoline motor with volume 170 ccm designed for being integrated in UAV.

It is a 4-stroke propulsion system with OHV and 2 valves per cylinder. The engine is equipped with a
microprocessor ignition for easy starting and smooth running in all modes of engine speed.

The power plant has been modified by UAVOS to improve performance :
* Air cooling and a two-nozzle fuel injection system have been made.
* A brushless generator-starter is installed on the engine.

UAVOS's injection system can be very precisely tuned with a lambda probe depending on the operating
conditions.

### FEATURES
* The engine is equipped with a fuel injection system
* 95-octane petrol + Valvoline 2T SynPower 30:1
* Maximum engine power: 9.3 HP (6.8 kW)
* Nominal engine power: 6.1 HP (4.5 kW)
* Fuel consumption: 320 g/kWh
* Forced air-cooling
* Equipped with starter-generator, 27V 3-phase AC motor. Generator power 500W up to 4800 rpm
* Total engine weight with ECU (engine control unit): 8.5 kg
* Maximum CHT operating temperature: 165 °C

### GENERAL DIMENSIONS

### PERFORMANCE PLOTS

Power to Torque relationship plot (OAT 15 °C, Atm.pressure 1013 mbar).

CHT to Power relationship plot at nominal RPM (OAT 15 °C, Atm.pressure 1013 mbar).

CHT to Throttle Position relationship plot at nominal RPM until overheating (OAT 15 °C, Atm.pressure
1013 mbar).

### ENGINE CONTROL UNIT

Engine is equipped with Engine Control Unit (ECU) UV01.6401.06.63.00.
This unit is intended for processing information from sensors:
* calculates the optimal amount of the fuel input;
* determines the moment of ignition (based on the operating conditions of the engine and its mode).

The unit is equipped with a digital data line, which allows the flight controller to transmit sensor
readings, as well as receive ignition commands and gas levels.
The main functions of the Engine Control Unit (ECU) UV01.6401.06.63.00:
* adjustment of the amount of fuel input;
* ignition timing adjustment;
* power supply control of the fuel pump;
* temperature measurements EGTх2, CHTх2, AT;
* the formation of control pulses of the gas servo drive;
* data exchange with a software navigation system.

**Electrical characteristics of the engine control unit**

**Supply voltage:**

12 ± 0.5 V

**Consumption current (no more)
(excluding nozzle current and fuel pump):**

0.5 A

**Ambient temperature:**

from -40°C to +60°C

**Relative humidity:**

up to 98% at 25°C

**Data transmission channels:**

CAN bus, discrete signal management

# GSG 140T GIMBAL

## Three-axis gyro-stabilized gimbal for night surveillance

### OVERVIEW

Gyro-stabilized 3-axis gimbal with thermal LWIR 640x512 camera. The optoelectronic onboard unit is
designed to perform complex missions and is ideally suited for a wide range of applications,
including inspections, security and law enforcement, surveillance, border control.

### FEATURES
* Weight: 1.2 kg
* Housing: aluminum
* IP-65
* Drying cartridge
* Direct drive
* Absolute encoder
* Angle of rotation: roll — +/- 30°, yaw — 360°, pitch — +/- 100°
* Coordinates measurement accuracy: 20-30 m
* Transmission of target coordinates to GCU
* Video output: Ethernet
* Operational temperature range: -40 … +50°C
* Supply voltage: 8-25V
* Max. power consumption: 40W
* Max. dimensions (length, diameter): 172.6x137mm
* Vibration-proof frame
* Rotation speed: 120°/sec

**Spectral Range:**

8 µm – 14 µm

**Thermal sensitivity:**

< 50 mK

**HFOV ﬁeld of view:**

63° (35 mm)

**Pixel size:**

17 µm

**Matrix resolution:**

640x512

**Effective frame rate:**

50Hz

# SITARIA E

## Fixed-Wing Unmanned System
## including the SITARIA aircraft and its GCS

Gallery ][15]
Video ][16]

### OVERVIEW

The **SITARIA** is a fixed-wing unmanned electric aircraft with full automatic takeoff, landing and
mission modes.

Diagnostics, flight mission planning and remote control can be performed through the wireless
network connection.

Proprietary Autopilot.

The operating time of the UAV is 3+ hours, depending on the height and operating conditions.

The aircraft uses a unique aerodynamic scheme allowing to quickly change the position of the wing
relative to the fuselage when the weight of the payload changes.

UAV empennage does not get into the jet from the propeller, thereby the resistance and vibration
decrease.

When the directional rudders deflect, a positive upsetting moment appears, which reduces the
necessary deviations of the ailerons. Aircraft controllability increases.

The specific weight of such empennage is minimal, which reduces the moment of inertia of the
aircraft, thereby improving controllability.

Command link: up to 100 km
Video transmission: up to 60 km (optional)
The Iridium backup command link is of unlimited range.

**Application:**
* Mapping
* Video surveillance and monitoring
* NDVI index agriculture
* Payload (max. 10 kg)
* Radio link relay

# TWO-BLADED MAIN ROTOR with All-metal Edging

## to be installed on helicopters with up to
## 50 kg take-off mass and rotor diameter
## of 2600 mm (102.36")

Gallery ][15]

### OVERVIEW

The state-of-the-art carbon main rotor blades are produced with latest carbon multi- cross-layer
technology using a curing oven.

The highly efficient carbon main rotor blades have been designed by gluing an all-metal edging into
the leading edge. The blades are fully interchangeable and carry a life-limit of 2,600 hours.

Due to the industrial production process the main rotor blades have long-life endurance, the
enhanced aerodynamic performance, the increased wear resistance under severe weather conditions. The
blades have superior behavior under extreme maneuvers.

### SPECIFICATIONS

**Length:**

1230 mm

**Width:**

76-38 mm

**Thickness:**

12.5-4.5 mm

**Root thickness:**

12.5 mm

**Mounting Hole Size:**

6 mm

**Rotation:**

Left (CCW) or right (CW)

**Twist:**

10°

**Material:**

Carbon fiber (prepreg), metal

**Max. RPM:**

1300

**Weight:**

0.42 kg

**MTOW (2 blades):**

50 kg

## ALPIN UNMANNED HELICOPTER

## a joint project of TITRA, a Turkish
## engineering company, and UAVOS

Gallery ][15]
Video ][16]

Alpin VTOL UAS has been created in accordance with the needs and requirements of the Turkish Rescue
& Security industry. The Alpin UAS is a long-range, heavy-lift unmanned helicopter capable of
carrying up to 160 kg with a range of up to 840 km. The converted Alpin UAS is based on the piloted
helicopter.

### ADVANTAGES

Night operations and flights under severe weather conditions
All terrain capable
Primed for ease operations
Meeting operational requirements
Low life cycle costs

Remote Ground Controls network capability
Simultaneous multi-UAV operation
Customizable software and SDK
Auto-rotation landing capability and high efficiency flight control, based on TECS
Redundant autopilot system

Payload Options:
* EO/IR
* RADARS SAR/GMTI
* LIDAR
* HYPERSPECTRAL

### APPLICATION
* Video surveillance and monitoring
* Autonomous cargo transportation and delivery
* Cargo dropping up to 160 kg (353 lbs) at specified location
* Radio relay
* Agricultural operations using spraying equipment
* Flying R&D laboratory (meteorology, hydrology, earth monitoring, etc.)

# ALBATROSS 2.2

## Fixed Wing UAV

Gallery ][15]
Video ][16]

Medium Altitude Long Endurance (MALE) UAS with a long flight duration about 20h with 88 lb (40 kg)
payload.

### OVERVIEW

The aircraft is designed for long-endurance missions in conditions of high turbulence and overloads.
The reinforced fuselage and landing gear are engineered for harsh landings, including on grass
airfields or prepared sites.
Take-off, route flight, and landing are carried out in fully automated mode.
Proprietary Autopilot.
The ALBATROSS UAV is equipped with satellite communication data link for Beyond Line of Sight
(BVLOS) operation.
Resistance to jamming.

### BENEFITS

Low cost of flying hour

The reliability of certified devices increases the reliability of the entire UAV system as a whole

The availability of a large network of dealer centers and spare parts stores

The conversion reduces the production time for an UAV

### APPLICATION
* Day and Night operations
* Cargo delivery
* Locating poachers and unauthorised activity in National Parks and other wildlife areas
* All kinds of Surveillance including communications interception
* Disaster Help – Civilian Support
* Maritime/Coastal Patrol
* SAR Operation and Victim discovery

# pMDDLRadio
# DATA LINK SYSTEM

## an advanced high power
## long range broadband COFDM
## communication system for UAV

### OVERVIEW

The pMDDLRadio Digital Data Link is a miniature, high power, long range broadband COFDM complete
wireless solution. Based on the new Microhard pMDDL core, it provides the bandwidth and range needed
for complex data intensive applications. The pMDDLRadio features 1W 2X2 MIMO 2.4GHz, using Maximal
Ratio Combining (MRC), Maximal Likelihood (ML) decoding and Low-Density Parity Check (LDPC) to
achieve robust RF performance.

The miniature, lightweight and rugged design is a reliable communication partner for unmanned
applications, both UAS and USV. The high speed, long range capabilities of the pMDDLRadio allow
simultaneous high quality duplex transmission of full HD video and control \ telemetry data.

Typical range with skew planar wheel antennas is 9 km [6 mi], longer range (up to 200 km [124 mi])
is available using high gain antennas / RF amplifiers / automatic tracking masts.

Typical set for 8-9 km range includes:

— 2x on-board omni-directional 5 dBi antennas (30 g x 2 / 0.066 lb x 2)

— 2x ground panel LAN antennas 14 dBi (430 g x 2 / 0.95 lbs. x 2)

— Drone and ground modems in the same design

— Required companion connectors

— Antenna cables

— Required LAN / RS cables (details TBD with customer)

### APPLICATIONS
* Unmanned BVLoS missions
* Emergency communication deployment
* Ethernet Wireless Extension
* Wireless Telemetry
* Wireless Video
* Wireless Control Systems

### FEATURES
* 2X2 MIMO high power 1W COFDM RF output
* External RF amplifiers support
* Rigid-Flex IMU board support
* Automatic tracking antenna support
* MicroSD for telemetry data recording (aka Black-box)
* RTC Clock with battery backup (200 hrs)
* Data Rates > 25 Mbps
* Adjustable Total Output Power (up to 1W)
* Maximal Ratio Combining (MRC)
* Maximal Likelihood (ML) decoding
* Low-Density Parity Check (LDPC)
* Small Footprint
* Lightweight
* Point-to-Point, Point-to-Multipoint
* Master, Remote, Relay (Future) Modes
* Low Power Consumption
* Simultaneous IP & Serial Data

### MODEM SPECIFICATION
* Duplex transmitter and receiver (2xMIMO)
* Dual MIMO antenna ports
* Operating range up to 8 km [5 mi] line-of-sight (The range depends on an ambient condition,
electromagnetic situation, radio interference within the area. In case automatic tracking mast is
not used, the range is guaranteed only within the HFOV of antenna)
* Frequency range: 2.402 - 2.478 GHz
* Encryption: 128-bit AES (Optional)
* Software selectable output power from 7 dBm to 30 dBm
* Up to 25 Mbps IPerf Throughput @ 8 MHz channel (-78 dBm)
* Up to 2 Mbps IPerf Throughput @ 4 MHz channel (-102 dBm)
* Software selectable MIMO on/off

### INTERFACES AND PORTS
* Serial Data/Console: 1 x transparent 3.3V TTL UART 300bps to 921kbps (Pixhawk support)
* Ethernet: Dual 10/100BaseT IEEE802.3 (LAN/WAN)
* Serial data prioritized over video data and has better sensitivity (additional modulation codes)
* STM32H743/53 onboard system controller with 4Mbit MRAM (allows customization of interfaces)
* Designated controller for automatic directional tracking antenna system (2 or 3-axes)
* External RF amplifiers support (provision for manual or automatic Tx/Rx switching)
* SPI interface: Rigid-Flex IMU board connection support (AHRS for tracking antenna & autopilot)
* Firewall: Port Forwarding, Access Control, IP/MAC List
* Diagnostics: Remote Diagnostics, Ping, Traceroute, ARP table, DHCP active leases, IPerf, RSSI
* Management: Local Serial Port Console, Telnet, WebUI, SNMP, FTP Upgrade, TFTP, CLI
* Designated interfaces for communication with autopilot, control system and ground station:
— 2 x CAN
— 1 x RS422
— 1 x RS485/RS232
— 1 x USB2.0
— GPIO: 8 x GPIO through transceiver, 4 x GPIO through level shifter
— Differential analog input: 1

### MECHANICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL FEATURES

##### ENCLOSED VERSION
* Weight, modem only: 90 g [0.198 lb]
* Dimensions: 90.5x70.7x18.2 mm [3.56x2.79x0.72 in]
* Sealed enclosure: rugged anodized aluminum-alloy
* Integrated pressure balance valve
* Ingress protection: meets IP65
* Temperature: -40°C to +50°C [-40°F to +122°F]
* Humidity: 95%, non-condensing
* Military connectors: Harwin M80 and RF - Hirose

### POWER FEATURES
* Full modem output power (30 dBm) at wide range of input voltage: 5-58 VDC
* Maximum power consumption @30 dBm in 2xMIMO mode and full process load: 10W
* Overvoltage protection: 58-80 V @5s of stable operation.

# AP 10.1

## Automatic Control System for UAV with a takeoff weight of 100 kg up to 4000 kg

### OVERVIEW

The Automatic Control System (AP) provides the hardware and vehicle control abstraction layer for
the host platform enabling fully autonomous operation. All flight systems including take-off,
landing, navigation and mission execution can be instigated with a single keystroke. All
diagnostics, flight mission planning and remote control can be achieved wirelessly.

A notable feature of the AP is its distributed architecture. Each component of the system has a
dedicated microcontroller providing data and communication with other components within the CAN bus.
This decentralized configuration helps to manage central processor loading by distributing routine
management tasks across all system components. Additionally, there are no restrictions on the number
of same-type modules connected to one system, enabling multiple redundancy on all levels. With
nearly all payloads or ready-made third-party modules, entire systems can be connected to the AP.

##### **FLEXIBILITY & SCALABILITY**

Thanks to the AP’s distributed architecture, the system can be used in a wide variety of vehicles
ranging from small quadcopter to full size converted piloted aircraft. The redundant layering
provides basic functionality while ground control software is multi-platform and functions across
multiple workstations in a both a wide or local area network configuration. Specific
payloads/sensors can be integrated by scripting custom protocols through onboard Virtual Machines
(VMs).

##### **COMPATIBILITY**

The AP is compatible with almost any vehicle configuration (VTOLs, USVs, UGVs, etc.), including
non-traditional aircraft concepts. The flight control algorithm relies on Total Energy Control
System (TECS) for improved reliability and response to malfunction including automatic landing with
engine failure, auto-rotation for helicopters and parachute deployment. The AP is resilient against
jamming and features precise dead-reckoning navigation in absence of a GNSS signal.

Payload of almost any type can be connected and controlled using the interfaces:
* 1-Wire
* RS-232
* RS-485
* UART
* CAN

### KEY FEATURES
* control of actuating mechanisms
* engine control
* semi-automatic control with automatic stabilization of the vehicles
* manual control using the main 928MHz communication channel
* from ground control station (GCU)
* control of the vehicles object in emergency mode
* payload control
* payload feedback
* control of rotating platforms in gyro-stabilization mode using AP10.1
* receipt and transfer of telemetric data between GCU and the vehicles
* simulation mode
* flight simulator
* onboard power control
* power stabilization
* conversion
* power distribution, including emergency power supply mode
* onboard power monitoring

### SPECIFICATIONS

### Available Interfaces:
* up to 15 x servo drives (PWM control)
* 2x inputs for RPM sensor (Hall-effect sensors)
* 1-Wire interface
* TTL UART interface
* RS-485 interface
* Controller area network - CAN
* RS-232 interface
* Low-side power output (3.7A, @ 20V, 68MOhm)
* 3x digital inputs (timing, level)
* 5x general purpose inputs-outputs (remappable on MCU)

# AP 10.2

## Automatic Control System for UAV with a takeoff weight of 15 kg up to 100 kg

### OVERVIEW

The **AP 10.2** system is designed to control a surface, ground or airborne platform automatically,
semi-automatically or manually.

The system is configurable for the following platforms:
* Standard airplane for automatic take-off and landing
* Rotor-wings for automatic take-off and landing
* Balloons, Blimps
* USVs (boats)
* UGVs (cars)
The **AP 10.2** was designed for small platforms and has the following advantages:
* reduced form factors (avionics weight less then 350 g)
* reduced energy consumption
Most payload can be interfaced through:
* 1-Wire
* RS-232
* RS-485
* TTL UART
* CAN

### KEY FEATURES
* Very small size and lightweight
* ESD protection
* Leading edge components and technologies
* Dead-reckoning, flight and navigation without GPS
* Automatic take-off and automatic landing
* Operating/flight mechanisms controls
* Engine/power plant control
* Semi-automatic control with automatic stabilization
* Manual control over 928MHz from ground control station
* Emergency mode
* Payload control
* Payload feedback
* Gyro-stabilization mode for rotating platforms
* Telemetry 10Hz with compressed stream, 100km LOS
* Ground simulation mode – flight simulator
* Operator training on flight simulator
* Pre-flight and flight assignment testing
* Onboard power control and monitoring
* Power stabilization
* Distribution, including emergency power supply mode

### SPECIFICATIONS

### Interfaces and characteristics:
* 12x servo drives (PWM outputs)
* 12x RPM sensor inputs (hall effect sensor)
* 1-Wire interface
* TTL UART interface
* RS-485 interface
* Controller area network - CAN
* RS-232 interface
* 4x Active-ground switched power output (4.7a, @ 27V, 68mOhm)
* 12x digital inputs (timing, level)
* 12x general purpose inputs-outputs (remappable on MCU)

# ApusDuo aircraft

ApusDuo is a solar-powered stratospheric High Altitude Pseudo Satellite (HAPS), developed by UAVOS.
Its persistence enables a capability of flying continuously for months at a time, at around 20,000
m, above weather and conventional air traffic.

ApusDuo relies on solar energy, with the batteries charged in daylight to power overnight flight.

ApusDuo is aimed to provide a wide scope of applications in Connectivity, Earth observation,
Weather, Security, Natural Resources and Emergency Disaster management.

The ApusDuo HAPS project became part of **Mira Aerospace**.

To find out more about ApusDuo visit** ****[Mira Aerospace][15]**.

## with MTOW up to 45 kg

Gallery ][15]

### OVERVIEW

The UVH 170 is an industrial grade helicopter with a four-stroke gasoline engine equipped with an
injector and a generator – starter.
Take-off and landing as well as mission are carried out automatically.
Optional semi-automatic control.
Emergency operation modes.
Diagnostics, flight planning and remote control can be performed via a wireless network connection.
Proprietary Autopilot.
The UVH 170 was specially designed with better engine cooling to perform in a tropical climate in a
hot and moist environment.

* Payload delivery
* Radio link range extension and retransmission
* R&D flying laboratory (meteorology, hydrology, earth monitoring, etc.)

Payload delivery (max. 5 kg)

Radio link range extension and retransmission

R&D flying laboratory (meteorology, hydrology, earth monitoring, etc.)

# SERVO ACTUATOR
# XSERVO140

Video ][15]

### OVERVIEW

Xservo-Series lightweight, Hollow Shaft Servo Actuators features embedded CANopen / EtherCAT servo
drive.

The advantage of this series is:
— the built-in motion controller, which allows the customer to skip the complex stage of mechanical
and electrical integration of a passive servo actuator with an external servo drive controller
— a versatile hollow shaft that makes it easy to pass power supply cables, shafts or laser beams
directly through the servo actuator.

New actuators are immune to shock and vibration and designed for use in harsh conditions.

### APPLICATIONS
* Automation and robotics
* Power movement of UAV control surfaces and elements

### SUPPORTED CONTROL MODES
* Cyclic Synchronous Position
* Cyclic Synchronous Velocity
* Cyclic Synchronous Torque
* Profile Position
* Profile Velocity

### SERVO ACTUATOR TELEMETRY DATA
* Position, speed
* Supply Voltage
* Current (RMS, Phase)
* Motor & power stage temperature

### SERVO ACTUATOR FEATURES
* Hollow shaft1
* Electromagnetic brake
* Shunt braking resistor
* Reverse polarity protection

¹hollow shaft that makes it easy to pass power supply cables, shafts or laser beams directly through
the servo actuator.

* Fully integrated video auto-tracker

* High-quality onboard video record

# PTP140

## Pan Tilt Platform

Video 1 ][15]
Video 2 ][16]
Video 3 ][17]

### OVERVIEW

The heavy-duty precision Pan Tilt Platform is a two - axis positioning system designed to withstand
harsh and extreme environmental and weather conditions.

State-of-the-art built-in control electronics and algorithms provide precise, smooth motion at all
speeds, while an integrated slip ring allows continuous rotation of the pan axis.

The body of the unit is made of high quality painted aluminum (or Saltwater Resistant Aluminum
Alloy) with rugged hermetic circular military connectors.

### APPLICATION
* Two-axes platform for balanced payloads up to 130 kg
* Payloads types: EO/IR, Antenna, Laser and similar systems

### SUPPORTED CONTROL INTERFACES & PROTOCOLS
* Ethernet (EtherCAT)
* CAN (CANopen, CANaerospace)
* RS422/485 (Modbus)
* Profile Position
* Profile Velocity

### FEATURES
* Hollow shaft for cables
* Electromagnetic brake for each of the axes
* Two-axes Gyro Stabilization (possible on request)
* GPS/GNSS True Heading (possible on request)

# MAIN LANDING
# GEAR

## to be installed on unmanned aircraft
## weighing up to 1200 kg

Video ][15]

### OVERVIEW

An advanced Main Landing Gear supporting aircraft weight up to 1200 kg.

The Main Landing Gear absorbs shocks that occur when the unmanned aircraft lands or runs over the
uneven surface of a runway.

The Main Landing Gear is made of aircraft prepreg carbon by the high-temperature molding procedure,
which makes it much stronger, thinner and lighter by 38% in comparison with fiberglass.

The Main Landing Gear weights 19 kg.

# Automated Drone Delivery Technology Solutions

## Docking Stations - A2Z AirDock

### AirDock Dual & AirDock Quad

Designed to blend seamlessly into a built environment, the multi-drone elevated AirDocks support
multiple stakeholders executing simultaneous missions across a joint area of operation.

[ Learn more ][27]

### AirDock Portable

Easily transportable and deployable within minutes, the AirDock Portable folds small and can be hand
carried. Deploy a single AirDock Portable or multiple to extend the Longtail’s serviceable area.

[ Learn more ][28]

### AirDock Shelter

Featuring a motorized clamshell dome, the AirDock Shelter houses one Longtail – AirDock Edition for
prolonged periods and can withstand extreme weather conditions.

[ Learn more ][29]

## Drone Systems

### Longtail Cargo - AirDock Edition

Designed to seamlessly integrate with the AirDock system, the Longtail Cargo – AirDock Edition
features automatic battery charging for round-the-clock autonomous operations. Built on a rugged
all-weather hexacopter platform, it delivers dependable performance in demanding logistics and
delivery environments.

[ Learn more ][30]

### Longtail Patrol - AirDock Edition

Designed for long-duration surveillance missions, the Longtail Patrol – AirDock Edition features
seamless integration with the AirDock for fully autonomous launch, recovery, and battery charging.
Equipped with a specialized patrol payload, it delivers consistent aerial monitoring and real-time
situational awareness for mission-critical operations.

[ Learn more ][31]

## Drone DELIVERY Winch AND ACCESSORIES

### RDS2 Drone Delivery Winch

Our second-generation Rapid Delivery System, the RDS2 offers the highest payload capacity of any
drone winch system on the market safely delivering up to 10 kg from altitude. Eliminating the need
for specialty payload boxes, the RDS2 gives drone delivery operators more flexibility in the shape,
size and weight of payloads they can carry.

[ Learn more ][32]

A compact, NDAA-compliant, DIU Blue approved industrial drone. Reliable, flexible and ready for your next mission. Learn More

WingtraRAY
Wingtra's all-new VTOL survey drone with 40% faster data capture, 61MP mapping, survey-grade accuracy, zero GCPs, and same-day deliverables. Learn More

DJI Matrice 400
DJI M400 offers 59-minute endurance, 6 kg payload capacity, power-line LiDAR /

radar sensing, 04 video transmission, and IP55 rugged reliability for missions. Shop Now

ACSL SOTEN
Japan's ACSL SOTEN delivers NDAA compliance, dual-band connectivity, new TAITEN smart controller, and mission-ready swappable payloads for mapping, thermal, and multispectral use cases. Learn More

DJI Zenmuse L3 LiDAR
DJI's Zenmuse L3 combines LiDAR with a high-resolution RGB mapping camera, delivering real-time 3D data and centimeter-level accuracy. Shop Now

Emlid Reach RS4, RS4 Pro, & RX2
Meet Emlid’s all-new lineup: Reach RS4, RS4 Pro, and RX2. Next-gen GNSS with AR stakeout, image capture, all-band RTK, and rugged IP68 hardware for reliable, centimeter-level results. Now Available

CONSTRUCTION & SURVEYING
Drones in construction and surveying empower AEC professionals to create virtual site surveys, develop detailed 3D models, and monitor project progress. LEARN MORE

MINING
Drones in mining empower industry professionals to enhance safety, optimize ore extraction, and monitor infrastructure efficiently. Learn more

PUBLIC SAFETY
Drones revolutionize public safety by enhancing situational awareness and enabling targeted responses. First responders on the ground benefit from real-time data to better assess and manage emergencies. LEARN MORE

AGRICULTURE
In precision agriculture, drones offer unparalleled crop monitoring, resource management, and data-driven insights. Farmers can increase yields, reduce environmental impact, and optimize overall efficiency. LEARN MORE

ENERGY & UTILITIES
Drone inspections are rapidly becoming the standard protocol for assessing critical infrastructure in the energy and utilities sector. Companies can safely and efficiently inspect assets, reducing downtime and ensuring reliability. LEARN MORE

Your Trusted Partner for Commerical & Enterprise Drones

At Advexure, we specialize in providing cutting-edge drone technology to empower businesses, public safety agencies, and enterprise users. Since our founding, we’ve partnered with law enforcement, fire departments, search and rescue teams, construction professionals, utility inspectors, and educators to deploy reliable, innovative unmanned aerial systems (UAS) tailored to their unique needs.

## Who we are

****Azansys Technologies LLP** is a next-generation drone manufacturing company driving innovation
in aerial technology for diverse industries across India. Headquartered in India, we specialize in
designing, developing, and delivering high-performance drones for **agriculture, logistics, mapping,
surveillance, and emergency response.

**With a dedicated team of engineers, innovators, and aviation experts, we are committed to
reshaping how the world sees and uses drones — not just as flying machines, but as intelligent tools
for progress.

[ Contact Us ][20]
[Drone Technology][Innovation]
[Solutions]

## Why Choose Azansys?

### Custom Solutions

Drones tailored to your mission—whether agricultural, industrial, or governmental.

### Make in India

Designed, developed, and manufactured locally for maximum reliability.

### R&D Driven

Innovations in AI, navigation, and battery systems for better efficiency and performance.

### Comprehensive Support

Deployment training, technical assistance, and lifecycle maintenance.

[Our Team]
10+
Years Experience

### Our Vision

► To become India’s most trusted and technologically advanced drone company, revolutionizing
industries and empowering solutions from the sky.

### Our Mission

►To design and manufacture **affordable, reliable, and high-performance drones**.
►To solve real-world problems in **agriculture, logistics, security, and environmental monitoring**.
►To contribute to a **safer, smarter, and more sustainable future** using aerial automation.

## Smart Drone Solutions for a Smarter World

At Azansys Technologies, we design and deliver advanced drone solutions for agriculture,
surveillance, mapping, logistics, and more. Our mission is to empower industries with intelligent,
reliable, and made-in-India drone technology that transforms operations on the ground and in the
air.

### Innovation in the Sky

We build cutting-edge drones designed to solve real-world problems across industries — with
precision, performance, and smart automation.

### Industry-Focused Solutions

Our drones are custom-designed for specific applications like crop monitoring, search and rescue,
industrial mapping, and aerial surveillance.

[Security Icon]

### Reliable & Rugged

We deliver dependable drones built for challenging environments — tested for endurance, accuracy,
and mission-critical operations.

Their Fleet Robotic Framework enables intelligent, coordinated drone swarms for applications in emergency response, infrastructure monitoring, and tactical surveillance, catering to sectors such as law enforcement, defense, and disaster relief. By offering cost-effective and real-time intelligence, Fleetrf aims to improve safety, security, and resilience in communities.

# About us

**Global Mark** is a leading Ukrainian company specializing in modern MilTech solutions. We are an
official importer of Autel and DJI drones.
Our team's primary goal is to supply reliable products to the armed forces to enhance the
effectiveness of combat operations.
The company's experts design and develop proprietary MilTech systems and equipment.
Global Mark offers advanced technological solutions at an affordable price with a quality guarantee.
Mission and Values
[Our Mission and Values]

## Our Mission and Values

The mission of Global Mark is to provide maximum support and equipment to the Ukrainian army with
MilTech solutions.

Our production is carried out in accordance with high standards of quality and reliability. We
implement effective and innovative systems into Ukraine’s defense complex that deliver maximum
results for the Armed Forces of Ukraine in combat operations and have been tested in real wartime
conditions.

integration and flight testing. Modern and advanced equipment and 3D printing capabilities are

across multiple usecases from industrial grade UAVs to compact consumer drones used in agriculture,

lightweight composite materials.

technology. As a leading **agriculture drone company in Tamilnadu**, with a strong focus on
precision, performance and reliability, our team blends technical expertise with a deep

### Kari Motor Speedway

[Site Survey]

###### OVERVIEW

## Drone Survey And Digitization Of Kari Motor Speedway, Coimbatore

The Kari Motor Speedway is a prominent racetrack in South India, known for hosting major domestic
and international motorsport events and training professional racers.
* **Industry**: Motorsport
* **Location**: Chettipalayam, Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu

###### Approval Efficiency

## Challenge: Time-Consuming Track Documentation and Approval Process

Before SKYX Aerospace’s involvement, the Kari Motor Speedway faced a significant challenge in
documenting track changes for approvals.
* Any modification to the track layout required extensive manual data collection, report
preparation, and submission to governing bodies.
* The process was time-intensive, taking 3 months or more for approvals due to the lack of precise
visual data and accurate elevation information.
* The absence of detailed aerial documentation made it difficult to assess elevation changes, corner
banking, and critical track elements effectively.

##### Our Solution: Drone-Based Survey and Digitization

SKYX Aerospace deployed its drone survey team at the racetrack for two days, covering an area of
over 50 acres. The captured data was then processed within the next two days, ensuring a fast and
efficient turnaround.

## Our comprehensive deliverables included

### Ortho-Rectified Image (GSD < 3cm)

High-resolution aerial image with a Ground Sampling Distance of less than 3cm, allowing precise
inspection down to 3cm objects.

### Digital Elevation Model (DEM) and Contour Maps

Provided detailed insights into track elevation, corner inclines, and elevation shifts.

### Survey Drawing with Markings

Includes Start/Finish Line, Pit Lane, Marshal Posts, Exits, Corners, and more.

### 2D KML, 3D KML and Geotagged KML Files

Enables remote visualization with detailed data layers in Google Earth Pro, enabling users to click
on labels and view additional details.

### 3D Model

Delivered for VR simulations, driver training, and marketing animations.

[Site Survey]

###### Impact

## Faster Documentation & Approval Process
* The previous 3-month approval timeline has now been reduced to just a few days.
* The management team now has high-resolution visual data that allows them to make informed
decisions quickly.
* The new 3D model and immersive VR experience are now enhancing visitor engagement and driver
training programs.

##### Conclusion

By leveraging SKYX Aerospace’s drone technology, the Kari Motor Speedway has revolutionized its
documentation process, improved operational efficiency, and enhanced the overall experience for both
stakeholders and racing professionals.

###### OVERVIEW

## Breathing New Life Into Namakkal Fort With Drones

Preserving history is no easy feat — especially when it’s carved into a 200-foot-tall rock formation
like the Namakkal Fort. When the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) wanted to document this iconic
site, they faced a daunting challenge — a process that would typically demand 14-18 personnel
working for an exhausting 30 days.
* **Industry**: Archaeology
* **Location**: Namakkal, Tamil Nadu

But at SKYX Aerospace, we believe in smarter solutions. We set out to prove that with drone
technology, this seemingly impossible task could be done faster, better, and with incredible
precision.

###### The SKYX Mission

## Precision Meets Efficiency
* On a crisp morning at 5:00 AM, our 2-person team set off from Coimbatore with just one drone and a
few DGPS instruments.
* By 8:30 AM, we were standing at the base of Namakkal Fort — coffee still warm in hand — preparing
to rewrite how heritage documentation is done.
* We carefully placed Ground Control Points across strategic locations to ensure precision down to
the centimeter. Once the setup was complete, it was time for the magic to begin.

##### The Drone Takes Flight

With every parameter dialed in and pre-flight checks passed, our drone soared into the sky,
following an autonomous flight path designed to capture the fort in stunning detail.

It didn’t just hover and snap pictures — it executed complex flight patterns for maximum coverage:
* Grid Flights for high-resolution mapping.
* Orbit and Spiral Patterns to capture the intricate rock formations from every possible angle.
* Multi-Angle Photography to ensure depth, texture, and structure were documented with incredible
clarity.

In less than half a day, the drone had gathered every detail that would’ve otherwise taken a manual
team 30 long days.

[Site Survey]

###### Data Transformation

## From Field to Data Lab - Fast Forward to Results

With data securely copied from the drone’s SD card, our field team relayed the files back to our
Data Processing Team in Coimbatore. While our data experts took over, the field team moved to their
next mission — knocking out three sites in just one day.

Meanwhile, our GIS analysts began stitching the captured data into a highly accurate Digital Twin of
the fort.

**They meticulously processed:**
* Noise Reduction – Eliminating unwanted data for pristine clarity.
* QA/QC Inspections – Ensuring every pixel matched reality.
* Precision Mapping – Creating outputs accurate enough to measure down to centimeters.

By the end of Day 2, ASI had everything they needed – clear, precise, and powerful documentation –
in their hands.

##### Deliverables That Redefined Documentation

Our solution included a range of comprehensive outputs for ASI’s long-term use:
* **3D Model** — Offering a detailed, interactive replica of Namakkal Fort.
* **3D Animation** — Creating a cinematic walkthrough experience for both visitors and historians.
* ** VR-Ready Virtual Tours** — Enabling immersive exploration of the site from anywhere.
* **Accurate Measurement Data** — Allowing ASI to inspect dimensions and features without revisiting
the site.
* **Sectional Drawings** — Empowering restoration teams to analyze the monument’s structure with
ease.
* **Vandalism & Damage Detection** — Providing early insights for faster repairs.

##### The Results: A New Standard for Heritage Preservation

What once took 30 days was now achieved in just 2 days.

A team of 2 people replaced the need for 18 manual surveyors.

ASI gained faster approvals, reduced errors, and significant cost savings.

The results weren’t just faster — they were better, sharper, and more insightful than ever before.
The ASI team now had powerful tools that helped them inspect, analyze, and plan with ease —
transforming how heritage preservation is done.

##### Heritage Preservation, Redefined

At SKYX Aerospace, we don’t just fly drones — we deliver solutions that break barriers. Our Namakkal
Fort project didn’t just save time — it gave ASI a new vision of what’s possible with technology.

**History deserves precision. Innovation makes it possible.**

### Ottankuttai

[Site Survey]

###### OVERVIEW

## Rescuing Kaarakuttai A Forgotten Lake’s Revival With Drone Technology

Once a thriving water body, Kaarakuttai — a small yet vital lake in northern Coimbatore — had been
reduced to a shadow of its former self. Shrubs had claimed the shoreline, debris piled up along its
banks, and its water-holding capacity had dwindled.
* **Industry**: Water Conservation
* **Location**: Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu

But when Siruthuli, a renowned NGO dedicated to water conservation, joined hands with SKYX
Aerospace, the vision was clear — to breathe new life into Kaarakuttai using cutting-edge drone
technology.

This wasn’t just about mapping a lake – it was about uncovering hidden vulnerabilities, redefining
its potential, and ensuring it could hold its ground for years to come.

###### Mission

## Mapping the Forgotten Waters

Our mission began with a detailed Drone Mapping Survey to capture every corner of the lake. But this
wasn’t an ordinary mapping exercise — our objective was to unlock crucial insights that traditional
methods often overlook.

Armed with precision drones and advanced GIS technology, our team launched a mission with multiple
objectives:
* Total Area Mapping: Surveyed the lake’s entire perimeter to establish accurate boundaries,
identifying encroachments, structures, and vegetation.
* Elevation Analysis: Scanned both the lake bed and its surrounding landscape to detect subtle
elevation changes.
* Digital Twin Creation: Built a stunningly detailed 3D replica of Kaarakuttai to serve as a
reference for future
conservation work.
* Water Holding Capacity Analysis: Calculated the lake’s maximum capacity down to the last liter.
* Surplus Weir Identification: Simulated rainfall and water inflow patterns to identify the lake’s
spillover point.
* Water Flow Simulation: Predicted the lake’s natural water-filling behavior to spot potential weak
points.
* Bund Weak Point Identification: Used elevation data to flag vulnerable points in the bund that
could lead to structural failure and flooding.

##### From Data to Action: Turning Insights into Impact

Once our mapping was complete, the results revealed that the lake’s original capacity had been
drastically reduced. Shrubs, silt deposits, and unwanted structures were choking its potential.

The data we provided enabled Siruthuli and its partners to take targeted action:
* Dense shrubs were cleared.
* Unwanted structures were dismantled.
* Parts of the lakebed were carefully excavated to increase its capacity.

Every decision – from where to dig to which areas required reinforcement – was driven by data from
our drone survey.

[Site Survey]

###### Transformation Unveiled

## The Final Step: Showcasing the Transformation

Once the rejuvenation was complete, we deployed our drones once again to perform a Post-Rejuvenation
Mapping Survey.

The results were breathtaking.

Our second mapping not only showcased the increased storage capacity but also visually captured the
dramatic transformation of Kaarakuttai. By overlaying Before vs. After data, stakeholders could see:
* Areas that had been deepened to boost capacity.
* How the water flow path had improved.
* Weak points in the bund that had been successfully reinforced.

##### The Impact: Data-Driven Conservation Done Right
* Faster Project Execution: What would have taken weeks to survey manually was accomplished in just
one day with our drones.
* Enhanced Water Holding Capacity: Strategic excavation increased the lake’s storage potential —
ensuring more water for local communities.
* Improved Flood Prevention: Early detection of weak bund points allowed timely reinforcement,
protecting nearby areas from potential flooding.
* Smarter Conservation Strategies: The precise Before vs. After comparison provided a powerful tool
for stakeholders to showcase the project’s success to the public.

##### A Forgotten Lake, Now a Lifeline

Thanks to Siruthuli’s dedication and SKYX Aerospace’s technological expertise, Kaarakuttai is no
longer a neglected water body — it’s now a thriving ecosystem with renewed potential.At SKYX
Aerospace, we believe that data can drive transformation — and this project proved just that.

### Logistics – Tea Plantation

[Site Survey]

###### OVERVIEW

## Transforming Tea Plantations With Logistics Drones – A Game-Changer For Ooty’s Tea Industry

In the lush green hills of Ooty, the tea plantations stretch as far as the eye can see – a
picturesque sight hiding a silent struggle. For decades, the women laborers who pluck tea leaves
have endured exhausting uphill climbs carrying heavy sacks of freshly harvested leaves. Each step
they took cost them time, energy, and – most importantly – income.
* **Industry**: Logistics
* **Location**: Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu

At SKYX Aerospace, we knew there had to be a better way — and we found one.

###### Efficiency Struggles

## The Challenge: Time, Energy, and Lost Earnings

Tea plantations in Ooty thrive across steep hills and rugged terrain. Each morning, women laborers
are dropped off near their designated areas to begin plucking tea leaves.

The process seems simple — until their sacks are full.

Once a plucker fills her 25 kg sack, she faces a tough choice:
* Carry the heavy sack downhill to the nearest accessible road, drop it off, and climb back uphill
with an empty sack.
* Or climb uphill with the full load to deliver it to the collection point.

This back-and-forth routine drained their energy, ate away their working hours, and severely limited
their earnings. Since the women are paid per sack, the more time they spent carrying leaves, the
less they earned.

##### Our Solution: A Logistics Drone with a Purpose

To solve this, we introduced a custom-built Logistics Drone tailored for the plantation landscape.

The drone was designed to:
* Carry heavy payloads efficiently.
* Fly long distances with minimal energy consumption.
* Operate safely and reliably in unpredictable hill station weather.

How It Works:
1. When a worker’s sack is nearly full, she notifies the drone operator.
2. The operator flies the drone directly to the worker’s location using GPS coordinates.
3. The drone carries a rope with carabiner hooks attached.
4. The worker simply clips her filled sack onto the hook and signals the operator.
5. The drone lifts the sack and flies directly to the tea factory — no detours, no delays.

[Site Survey]

###### The Impact

## Redefining Productivity and Profitability
* Increased Factory Production: With leaves arriving at the factory faster and fresher, production
rates soared.
* Higher Earnings for Workers: Women laborers could now focus entirely on plucking more tea leaves
instead of wasting time carrying heavy sacks — directly boosting their income.
* Fresher Tea Leaves, Better Quality: By reducing transportation time, leaves retained their natural
oils and aroma — enhancing the quality of the final product.
* Reduced Fuel Consumption: Traditional methods relied on tractors frequently climbing up and down
the hilly terrain. With the drone, this need was drastically reduced.
* Shorter Distances, Faster Results: Air travel meant the drone could cut across hills — avoiding
winding roads and reaching the factory in a fraction of the time.

##### A New Era for Ooty’s Tea Industry

This innovation wasn’t just about technology – it was about empowering workers, saving time, and
improving quality.

In a region where tradition meets agriculture, SKYX Aerospace’s Logistics Drone has redefined what’s
possible – proving that sometimes, the best solutions aren’t just high-tech… they’re human-focused.

**The hills of Ooty now echo with something more than the rustling of tea leaves — they echo with
opportunity.**

# Medical Drone Delivery

Avion connects remote clinics with urban healthcare infrastructures, ensuring rapid, safe, and
efficient delivery of vital medical supplies and clinical samples to the most hard-to-reach
locations.

[Contact Us][5][Learn More][6]
Features

## Cutting-Edge Technology Platform

Our platform combines advanced autonomous drone technology with an intuitive digital health
interface

eVTOL Drones
Advanced autonomous drones with seamless take-off and landing capabilities, even in challenging
terrains.
Digital Health Platform
Intuitive interface connecting healthcare providers with labs and pharmacies in real-time.
Medical Supply Delivery
Rapid and safe delivery of vital medical supplies to remote locations.
Clinical Sample Transport
Efficient transport of clinical samples from remote clinics to sophisticated urban labs.
Real-Time Tracking
Track shipments and communicate with laboratory and pharmacy staff through our platform.
Safe & Secure
Ensuring the highest standards of safety and security for all medical deliveries.
How It Works

## Simple, Efficient Process

From order to delivery, our streamlined process ensures healthcare reaches where it's needed most

01
Place Order
Healthcare providers use our intuitive platform to order supplies or schedule sample transport
02
Drone Dispatch
Autonomous eVTOL drones are automatically dispatched with advanced route optimization
03
Real-Time Tracking
Monitor delivery progress in real-time through our digital health platform
04
Safe Delivery
Drones safely deliver to remote clinics or transport samples to urban labs
Benefits

Avion's innovative platform brings unprecedented advantages to healthcare delivery in remote areas.

Rapid delivery to hard-to-reach locations
24/7 autonomous operation capability
Real-time tracking and communication
Reduced delivery costs and time

Seamless integration with existing healthcare systems

# Home of Drones For Good®
# and AAM for Good**®**.

## We are America’s leading non-profit organization saving lives by advancing uncrewed aviation for
## public safety, emergencies, and disaster response.


[ Our Vision ][37]

**The Airborne International Response Team (AIRT) was founded with a single vision; to provide
innovative airborne capabilities that help people prepare for, respond to, and recover from complex
emergencies and major disasters.**

**Since our creation in 2017, AIRT programming has expanded to support public safety and emergency
services organizations across the U.S. and around the world to build and manage uncrewed aircraft
systems (UAS) programs. These resources protect property, restore critical infrastructure, and help
save lives.**

**As UAS technology proliferates, AIRT is evolving it’s Drones For Good® program through our newest
non-profit program, AAM For Good. Learn how you can get involved and support our Drones For Good®
and AAM For Good® missions!**

### Airborne International Response Team

Launched in 2017 as our flagship program, the Airborne International Response Team (AIRT) works with
domestic and international partners across all sectors to advance the use of uncrewed aircraft
systems (UAS) for emergency response, humanitarian assistance, and disaster relief (HA/DR).

[ Learn More ][38]

AIRT is the official home of the DRONERESPONDERS Program, established in 2019 as the world’s leading
non-profit program supporting public safety agencies and emergency services organizations using UAS
and related technology for life-safety missions in more than 85 countries.

[ Learn More ][39]
[ [2024 Florida Public Safety Drone Operations Conference] ][40]

Created in 2021, the Florida Public Safety Coordination Group (FLOGRU) serves as a model for states
to share information and knowledge about government drone operations between the public and private
sectors.

[ Learn More ][41]

AIRT’s Drones For Good® program is designed to educate target audiences about the many benefits of
solving problems using UAS and related technology for a wide range of use cases.

### ®

[ Learn More ][42]

Launched in 2024, AAM For Good is AIRT’s newest program uniting stakeholders across all sectors to
explore how the emerging advanced air mobility ecosystem can positively impact communities for
public safety, emergency services, humanitarian assistance, and disaster relief (HA/DR) missions.

[ Learn More ][43]

Partners

## “Drones and advanced aviation are shifting world how the world manages emergencies and
## catastrophes. AIRT is the thrust propelling the tip of that spear.”

— Christopher Todd, CEM®, EMPS, Executive Director, AIRT

# Home of Drones For Good®
# and AAM for Good**®**.

## We are America’s leading non-profit organization saving lives by advancing uncrewed aviation for
## public safety, emergencies, and disaster response.


[ Our Vision ][37]

**The Airborne International Response Team (AIRT) was founded with a single vision; to provide
innovative airborne capabilities that help people prepare for, respond to, and recover from complex
emergencies and major disasters.**

**Since our creation in 2017, AIRT programming has expanded to support public safety and emergency
services organizations across the U.S. and around the world to build and manage uncrewed aircraft
systems (UAS) programs. These resources protect property, restore critical infrastructure, and help
save lives.**

**As UAS technology proliferates, AIRT is evolving it’s Drones For Good® program through our newest
non-profit program, AAM For Good. Learn how you can get involved and support our Drones For Good®
and AAM For Good® missions!**

### Airborne International Response Team

Launched in 2017 as our flagship program, the Airborne International Response Team (AIRT) works with
domestic and international partners across all sectors to advance the use of uncrewed aircraft
systems (UAS) for emergency response, humanitarian assistance, and disaster relief (HA/DR).

[ Learn More ][38]

AIRT is the official home of the DRONERESPONDERS Program, established in 2019 as the world’s leading
non-profit program supporting public safety agencies and emergency services organizations using UAS
and related technology for life-safety missions in more than 85 countries.

[ Learn More ][39]
[ [2024 Florida Public Safety Drone Operations Conference] ][40]

Created in 2021, the Florida Public Safety Coordination Group (FLOGRU) serves as a model for states
to share information and knowledge about government drone operations between the public and private
sectors.

[ Learn More ][41]

AIRT’s Drones For Good® program is designed to educate target audiences about the many benefits of
solving problems using UAS and related technology for a wide range of use cases.

### ®

[ Learn More ][42]

Launched in 2024, AAM For Good is AIRT’s newest program uniting stakeholders across all sectors to
explore how the emerging advanced air mobility ecosystem can positively impact communities for
public safety, emergency services, humanitarian assistance, and disaster relief (HA/DR) missions.

[ Learn More ][43]

Partners

## “Drones and advanced aviation are shifting world how the world manages emergencies and
## catastrophes. AIRT is the thrust propelling the tip of that spear.”

— Christopher Todd, CEM®, EMPS, Executive Director, AIRT

The company focuses on developing and deploying drones that can rapidly deliver medical supplies and equipment to critical locations, thereby improving response times in emergency situations. Its target market includes healthcare providers, emergency response teams, and organizations seeking to optimize medical logistics and patient care.

relevant_companies.polished_summary: Ambulance Drone Wins specializes in innovative drone technology aimed at enhancing emergency medical services. The company focuses on developing and deploying drones that can rapidly deliver medical supplies and equipment to critical locations, thereby improving response times in emergency situations. Its target market includes healthcare providers, emergency response teams, and organizations seeking to optimize medical logistics and patient care.

relevant_companies.company_summary: Droneresponders is a non-profit organization dedicated to enhancing public safety by uniting aerial first responders, emergency managers, and search and rescue specialists to optimize drone operations. The organization offers comprehensive training programs and online courses focused on UAS operations and safety, targeting emergency responders and public safety organizations as well as individuals and entities interested in drone training. Through its initiatives, Droneresponders aims to advance the effective use of drones in critical situations across the public safety, emergency management, and search and rescue sectors.

# OUR MISSION

# RESEARCH, TRAINING, EDUCATION & KNOWLEDGE

JOIN THE NETWORK

## WE ARE THE
## DRONERESPONDERS

Throughout the U.S. and around the world you see them launching unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) into
the sky during various types of emergencies and incidents. These are the DRONERESPONDERS, and our
ranks are growing every day as more organizations continue to embrace UAS for public safety
missions.

DRONERESPONDERS is a non-profit program created to unite these new aerial first responders,
emergency managers, and search and rescue specialists under a unified organization to help learn,
train, and test with one another with the ultimate objective of maximizing drone operations for
public safety.

The DRONERESPONDERS program is led by Chief Charles Werner (ret.) who serves as the director.
DRONERESPONDERS is an official 501(c)3 non-profit Drones for Good™ program of [AIRT][31], Inc.

# OUR MISSION

# RESEARCH, TRAINING, EDUCATION & KNOWLEDGE

JOIN THE NETWORK

## WE ARE THE
## DRONERESPONDERS

Throughout the U.S. and around the world you see them launching unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) into
the sky during various types of emergencies and incidents. These are the DRONERESPONDERS, and our
ranks are growing every day as more organizations continue to embrace UAS for public safety
missions.

DRONERESPONDERS is a non-profit program created to unite these new aerial first responders,
emergency managers, and search and rescue specialists under a unified organization to help learn,
train, and test with one another with the ultimate objective of maximizing drone operations for
public safety.

The DRONERESPONDERS program is led by Chief Charles Werner (ret.) who serves as the director.
DRONERESPONDERS is an official 501(c)3 non-profit Drones for Good™ program of [AIRT][31], Inc.

JOIN THE NETWORK

## BOARD OF ADVISORS

The DRONERESPONERS Board of Advisors are carefully selected to represented a cross-section of each
of the key stakeholders in the public safety UAS sector. Each advisor is appointed to a 1-2 year
term to ensure the organization remains at the forefront of the unmanned aviation evolution.

relevant_companies.polished_summary: Droneresponders is a non-profit organization dedicated to enhancing public safety by uniting aerial first responders, emergency managers, and search and rescue specialists to optimize drone operations. The organization offers comprehensive training programs and online courses focused on UAS operations and safety, targeting emergency responders and public safety organizations as well as individuals and entities interested in drone training. Through its initiatives, Droneresponders aims to advance the effective use of drones in critical situations across the public safety, emergency management, and search and rescue sectors.
